answer: Every ballot must live alone on its own island: inside a hardware vault — a Nitro Enclave or SGX enclave — sealed even from its owner. Each epoch, the tide brings a fresh attestation wave: every ballot presents a signed quote proving real silicon, one quote per CPU. A farm's 10,000 clones cram onto one machine, but AWS caps four enclaves per parent instance, so 9,996 clones present duplicate quotes and die — each forfeits a $25 bond, $249,900 vaporised, and 2,500 parent instances at $0.33 an hour. One island, one vault; a copied quote gets every ballot rejected and its bond burned.
